A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with readable text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E. Pages 2–32 are identical in extracted text and rendered appearance; differences are confined to the first page.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix E report original synthetic and semi-synthetic experiments and an empirical minimum-wage analysis, including MSE results and treatment-effect calibration plots.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix E retain the original simulation and minimum-wage analysis results, including Tables 1–7 and Figures 1–4.

M1.justification: The doubly robust CATT learner, covariate-shift framework, multi-period extension, and instrumented and lagged-outcome variants are unchanged (Sections 3–5; Appendices A–B).

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic data, imbalance and parallel-trends-violation scenarios, and semi-synthetic and real minimum-wage data (Section 6; Appendix E).

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical within corresponding experiments, including outcome regression, CATE outcome regression, CATE doubly robust learners, and lagged-outcome alternatives (Tables 1–7).

E3.justification: The held-out MSE evaluation, model configurations, treatment-probability reduction, sample construction, and calibration procedure remain unchanged (Section 6; Appendix E.1).

E4.justification: The analyses of imbalance, omitted controls, higher dimensionality, parallel-trends violations, and minimum-wage effect calibration are identical, including the supplementary evidence in Appendix E.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over 100 simulations or semi-synthetic datasets and retain the same calibration confidence intervals. Run-count and uncertainty-reporting information are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–7 and plotted results in Figures 1–4 are identical. For example, Table 3 retains the XGBoost (DR) Best-column MSE of 1.8 ± 0.09.

T1.justification: The identification assumptions, orthogonal moments, loss formulations, rate bounds, and mathematical derivations are unchanged, including all proofs and extensions in Appendices A–D.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same claims about doubly robust CATT estimation, general conditional functionals under covariate shift, instrumented DiD, and empirical superiority. Contribution scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: The explanations of robustness, qualifications concerning identifying assumptions, and interpretation of smaller negative employment effects in larger counties remain unchanged (Sections 3 and 6; Appendices B and E).

D1.justification: Model-fitting descriptions and synthetic and semi-synthetic data-generation details are identical (Section 6; Appendix E.1). The funding acknowledgment edit adds no implementation or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, comparisons with prior DiD and CATE research, and novelty positioning are unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page acknowledgment changes NSF Award IIS-2337916 support from Vasilis Syrgkanis alone to Vasilis Syrgkanis and Hui Lan, with corresponding grammatical adjustment. The arXiv version/date stamp also changes; the narrative and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The revised first-page funding acknowledgment causes limited line reflow in the funding/affiliation footnote, and the marginal arXiv stamp changes. All figures, tables, and layouts on pages 2–32 remain identical.

improvement.justification: v2 updates funding attribution and version/date information but leaves the scientific text, methods, theory, experiments, and appendices unchanged. These administrative edits and the small footnote reflow produce no meaningful difference in the paper's rigor, evidence, or clarity.
